CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  AUGUST  12, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  6:41 p.m.

mVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Ms. Griego,  LAUSD  Board  Member,  District  5

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston  City
  Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

GUEST  SPEAKER  Karla  Griego,  LAUSD  Board  Member,  District  5, acknowledged  the pain,
  suffering  and fear our communities  have endured  and experienced  in the
  past couple  of months,  especially  in the southeast  cities.  She too  is

  outraged  by the inhumane  attacks  on the irnrnigrant  communities  across
  Los Angeles  during  the last couple  of months.  Despite  these
  unprecedented  times,  she's seen the resilience  and perseverance  of
  families,  communities  and of councils  throughout  the southeast  cities.  It
  gives her hope because  that shows that better  times  are ahead. She thanked
  everyone  present,  Mayor  Davila,  who stood in solidarity  with  LAUSD
  yesterday  with  other city representatives  during  their  press conference.
  She is excited  and grateful  that the City  of South  Gate will  also be
  working  with  the district  to support  the students'  return  to school.  As a
  school  board member  representing  the students  in South  Gate, she shared
  what the LAUSD  has and what they are doing  to ensure a safe opening
  and return  to schools.

  Ms. Griego  invited  everyone  to their District  5 0ffice  open house,  on
  August  27'h at Gage Middle  School  from  4 to 6 p.m.

  Mayor  Davila  thanked  Ms. Griego  for being  here tonight  and sharing
  information.

  Councilwoman  Avalos  and Council  Member  Rios welcomed  Ms. Griego
  to South  Gate and enlighten  everyone  with  all the resources.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  has reached  out to Ms. Griego  few times  and
  she is very responsive.  He thanked  her for being  very responsive.

cugsrspyayncos'ron  Ms. Griego  stated that the whole  district  is her heart.  She is a 20 year
  teacher,  and teachers  love all their  students.  Her goal is to make sure the
  cornrnunities  get representation  and be heard.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  thanked  Ms. Griego  for being  here tonight  and

  providing  information.  This reassures  families  and members  of the
  community  that we have a school  district  taking  this seriously  and have

  created  a game plan to handle  these situations.

ITEMS

  Castillo  came before  City  Council  asking  for their  assistance  to permit

  their  group  to continue  gathering  at South  Gate Park doing  activities  on

  Tuesdays  and Thursdays.  For the last three weeks  they have been harassed
  by the South  Gate Park Ranger  that won't  allow  them  to continue  with

  their activities.  On a couple  of occasions,  the Park Ranger  has become  a

  little  aggressive.  The group  is not causing any harm or any grievance to
  the park. It was recommended  to the group to rent a soccer field, but they
  cannot  afford  it.

  Mayor  Davila  requested  Mr. Sanchez  give  Steve Costley  his number.

  Edgar  Pelayo,  South  Gate resident,  informed  the group  who just spoke that
  on Thursday  at 7:00 p.m. in this building,  we'll  have a Parks & Rec
  Commission  meeting. He thanked the chief  for answering  their  questions

  regarding  horses.  He also thanked  the officers  for providing  their time  and

  resources  for the horses.

  Mr. Pelayo  commented  on some concerns  from  people  that just  come,

  criticize  and don't  provide  any type of solution  to any of the issues going
  on in the city.

  Roberto  Sanchez  thanked  the city  for the pickle  ball strip lines at the South
  Gate tennis  courts.  He is recommending  using  one teru'iis court  for four

  pickle  ball nets.

EMAILS  Brenda  Rojas,  PhD,  South  Gate resident,  stated that GWS/UWS  a

  composting  facility  located  in the City  of South  Gate, has a history  of

  documented  odor and dust complaints  the city and South Coast Air
  with
  Quality Management  District  dating back at least 2015. On August 7,
  2025, Dr. Rojas confirmed  with  AQMD  supervisor  that recent odor
  complaints  have not been routed  to the local  enforcement  agency  as

  required  under  California  Health  and Safety  Code  41705.

  Roberto  Sanchez,  South  Gate resident,  requested  an update  on the virtual
  attendance  and participation  options  for city council  meetings.  He

  expressed  concern  over the city's  budget  deficit,  pointing  out inconsistent

  and complaints  not reaching  the proper  channels.  The resident
  recommends  the city distribute  a survey  to nearby  residents  and businesses

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROMCITYOFFICIALS  ArturoCervantes,DirectorofPublicWorks,nothingtoreport.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  commented  on community
  events.

  Gabriel  Perez, Director  of Community  Development,  informed  City
  Council  that staff is following  up on the concerns  regarding  order  or dust
  potentially  coming  from  UWS  or GWS.  The complaints  are getting  logged
  and veri'fying  those complaints  do come from  there or if it's another
  source.  The city is in communication  withAQMD.

  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  nothing  to report.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  nothing  to report.

  Chief Arakawa  reiterated  that the Police  Department  has plenty  of
  personnel  on duty that will  be able to assist school  police  if it's necessary.
  He also mentioned  six weeks  away  from  the South  Gate car show. The
  funds benefit  the toy drives.  Saturday,  September  6 the Pink Patch Project
  and LA County  Sheriff's  Department  have put together  a 5K Run at Frank
  Bonelli  Park in San Dimas.

  The Chief  attended  the funeral  services  for Detective  Lemus  from  the
  Sheriff's  Department.  He mentioned  that police  work  is a very dangerous
  job and the women  and men that protect  this community  and across LA
  County,  sometimes  they don't  know  if they will  be coming  home.
  Detective  Lemus  left behind  his wife  and three children.  He is asking  the
  public  to always  support  the police  officers.  It's easy to criticize  police
  officers  for one incident  that happens  in the Midwest  or on the other side
  of the country.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager,  reported  that HdL  will  be taking  over the
  business  license  process  this week.  There  will  be an online  portal  for
  people  to access instead  of coming  into city hall to apply  for a business
  license  or renew  their  business  license.

CONT'D  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney  reported  that today  the City  of South  Gate
  joined  about 20 other cities  in filing  an amicus  brief  before  the United
  States Supreme  Court.  The purpose  of the brief  was to the city's  position
  with  respect  to requesting  the Supreme  Court  to uphold  the stay order that
  was issued by a federal  district  court judge  in coru'iection  with  the
  irnrnigration  activities  and enforcement  activities  that were going  on. The
  district  court  issued a stay order. It appealed  to the ninth  circuit  which
  upheld  the district  court's  order.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  nothing  to report.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  stated that we encourage  our civic  engagement
  and welcome  residents  to participate  in our meetings.  While  we currently
  do not have a virtual  option,  she invites  everyone  to attend  in person  in the
  Council  Chambers  to share their  concerns  directly  or email  your
  comments  to her. She will  then forward  the comments  to the City  Council
  Members.

  Council  MemberAvalos  welcomed  everyone  present  tonight  and on
  YouTube.  She had an opportunity  to attend  the Southeast  Water Coalition.
  South  Gate joined  in a lawsuit  several  years ago with  3M and received  a
  report  from  the Council  from  New  Orleans  indicating  the city received
  some  monies  from  3M.  She would  like to know  how much  the city
  received.  The City  of Pico Rivera  received  $lmillion.

  Mr. Salinas  does not have the exact amount,  but perhaps  before  the City
  Council  Meeting  is up, he can get that information  for her.

  Council  MemberAvalos  stated that the Southeast  Water  Coalition  is
  opening  membership  to other cities that are water  providers  to their
  residents.  She will  be attending  Vector  Control  this Thursday.  She asked
  Mayor  Davila  for an update  on the HUB  Cities.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  welcomed  everyone  present  tonight.  He stated
  City  Council  receives  copies  of the emails  received  by the City  Clerk.  He
  stated that these are difficult  times  for everybody  due to the raids and
  doesn't  want to give anyone  false hope.

  Council  Member  Rios asked if the group  that was present  tonight  are using
  the wrong  place of the park.

  Mr. Costley  stated that when  organized  leagues  show up at a park without
  a permit  it becomes  a large liability  for the Parks & Recreation
  Department  and the city and some states laws that are not being  adhered
  to.

CONT'D  Council  Member  Rios  thanked  Mr.  Costley  for the explanation.  He asked
  if the city  could  do anything  regarding  ebikes  and other  motor  vehicles.

  ChiefArakawa  stated  that there  is lots of con:fusion  about  ebikes  even  in
  the legislature  because  they're  so new.  The bikes  that  don't  have  pedals
  but are electric  run vehicles  are technically  not legal  for the streets.

  Council  Member  Rios  thanked  the Chief.  He invited  everyone  to the open
  house  campus  tomorrow  on Santa  Fe Avenue  between  4:00  to 7:00  p.m.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  attended  both  events  at both  parks  and it was well
  attended.  He asked  Mr.  Houston  and Mr.  Perez  if the staff  are providing
  status  on the odor  and dust complaints  to the residents.

  Mr.  Houston  responded  that  staff  have  had communication  with  the main
  leader  of the neighborhood.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  thanked  Mr.  Houston  for providing  the invite  on
  August  Ist with  Assembly  Member  Jose Solache  at the Maywood  YMCA.
  Maywood  YMCA  was awarded/allocated  funds  to be able to offer
  resources  to local  cities.

  Mayor  Davila  stated  that  on Monday  at 4:00  p.m.  the new  local  LAUSD
  Superintendent,  Dr. Ortiz,  will  be having  a meeting  at South  Gate Middle
  School.  She will  not be attending  the County  Sanitation  meetings  because
  they  go dark  the whole  month  of August.  And  regarding  Councilwoman
  Avalos'  question  regarding  HUB  Cities,  HUB  Cites  is in the process  of
  contracting  a new  Interim  Director  because  the previous  director,  Joe
  Martinez  retired.  Andy  Pasmant  will  be the Interim  Director  and helping
  HUB  Cities  with  the finances.  Unfortunately,  HUB  Cities  did not get the
  grant  from  the county,  which  will  be appealed.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  mentioned  his son's  wife  is expecting  their  third
  child.

FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  Councilwoman  Avalos  stated she forgot  to speak on an item  earlier
CONT'D

  tonight.  She stated that as a Member  of the City  Council  she is formally

  requesting  a thorough  review and clarification  of the city's  relationship

  with  the Southeast  Junior  Athletic  Association.  This is based on recent
  resident  communication  and troubling  patterns  regarding  organizational

  behaviors  that she has significant  concerns  about transparency,
  governance,  and potential  legal and financial  exposure  to the city. It is

  unclear  the separation  the city and the organization.
  between  There is no

  documentation  that she has seen that clearly  defines  the  operation  or legal

  boundaries  between the city and this nonprofit  organization.  The lack of

  clarity has caused confusion  among some of the  residents  and  appears to

  blur some of the important  lines of responsibility.  Notably,  one of the

  residents  reached  out with  several  concerns  regarding  a refund  referred.

  They  asked Council  Member/Vice  Mayor,  and he basically  referred  this

  individual  to the Parks & Recreation  Director.  Why  was this referral  made

  to the Parks & Recreation  Director  directly?  Under what authority  is this

  direction  occurring,  and what  is the  city's  explanation  when elected

  officials  refer grievances  to municipal  staff. Staff should not be involved
  in their internal businesses or disputes. She is also recommending  this

  issue be placed  on the City  Council  agenda to allow  full  discussion,

  community  input,  and reassessment  of the appropriateness  of the

  relationship.  She has received  emails  from  this specific  resident  and a
  group  of parents.

  Mr. Salinas  advised  Councilwoman  Avalos  to direct  her requests  over to

  the City  Manager  because  of the City  Manager  for of government  as

  opposed  to having  anyone  from  direct staff. There are
  the Council
  limitations in the city's municipal  code. He  also  asked her to pass her
  notes that might have those inquiries  to the City Manager.
